target_customer: Engineering and security teams in regulated industries (finance, food delivery, healthcare) that deploy their own AI agents
problem: Security tools flag AI agent issues and file tickets, but teams in regulated industries need verified fixes and runtime checks of every agent action without slowing the business.
business_model: B2B SaaS for agent security assessment, fix verification and runtime protection (Armorer Guard), sold by demo
product_category: AI agent security and runtime guardrails

founders.name: Daniel Begimher
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: led the global Application Security technical field community at AWS and the AI investigative agent in AWS Security Incident Response; author of SIR-Bench and ASH. Education not listed.

founders.name: Cristian Leo
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: led AI security science at AWS; co-created ThreatForest. Education not listed.

competitors.name: Lakera Guard
competitors.what: Prompt injection and jailbreak detection API
competitors.traction_then: Established detector product per 2026 comparison guides

competitors.name: Datadog AI Guard
competitors.what: Per action evaluation inside the agent loop that blocks malicious activity

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs small CPU only detection models that beat other detectors on public benchmarks (company claim: 22 percent more accurate and 88 times faster than JEV), plus attack simulation and verified fix generation.

defensibility.rationale: Benchmark claims are self reported and the space has many funded guardrail vendors and cloud providers; SOC 2 and regulated industry trust could build switching costs later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; incumbents already shipped runtime guardrails by the Fall 2026 batch.

market_need_then: Enterprises were deploying agents in 2026 and security standards (OWASP Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF) were being mapped; a Just Eat Takeaway engineering director is quoted as a customer, but counts and revenue are not given.

branding.domain_note: Uses armorerlabs.com with the Labs suffix.

identity.visual_style: Enterprise security site with Trust Center and SOC 2 seal
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, contrasts with other tools, e.g. Most tools stop at findings. Armorer verifies fixes.

branding.brand_signature: Armorer Guard, an open source runtime guard with sub 2 ms latency claim
branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch evidence found; ThreatForest and SIR-Bench give the founders some security community credibility.

brand_strength.rationale: Pre launch brand; the name echoes defense and armor terms that crowd search results, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Armorer Labs is a Fall 2026 YC company that is active with two ex AWS founders. It targets a fast growing need for agent security in regulated firms but faces many funded guardrail vendors and cloud incumbents. No exit, funding round or revenue figure is verified, so the outcome is unresolved.
notes: Funding: Paul Vixie is named as advisor and investor on the YC page and company site, but the amount is not disclosed; a Dealroom entry lists a seed round with hidden amount. No round recorded. Competitor source dates are the year only (2026 comparison articles). Searches for outcome returned unrelated results, so no negative news was found rather than confirmed.
